Current Unfought

Current
Unfought

The tape is rolling, the weights overlap, and the checks are there to be signed. The only thing missing is the contract. Every fighter featured here claims the crown, but the definitive fights remain unmade — stalled by promotional walls, legal entanglements, or deliberate risk management. This section isn’t a museum; it’s a live audit. We hold the receipts here until someone has the nerve to step through the ropes and clear the ledger.

Super Middleweight · Current
Canelo Alvarez vs. David Benavidez
Duck Call: Canelo
Canelo Alvarez · David Benavidez · The fight the WBC buried

Benavidez became WBC mandatory at super middleweight in May 2022 after stopping David Lemieux in three rounds. The WBC extended that mandatory window — giving Canelo two full years of protection rather than the standard one — something his sanctioning body did not do for any ordinary champion. Canelo used that window to fight GGG III, Charlo, Munguia, Berlanga, and Scull. He captured all four world titles at 168 pounds without ever stepping in the ring with Benavidez, who was the consensus top super middleweight outside of Canelo himself.

When Benavidez ran out of runway, he moved up to light heavyweight, where he won a world title, then moved up again in May 2026, emphatically dethroning unified cruiserweight titlist Gilberto Ramirez in one of the standout performances of the year.

“Right now, it’s just impossible. He can come fight with heavyweights.” — Canelo, May 2026

The counter-argument writes itself: Canelo previously moved to light heavyweight to fight Sergey Kovalev and Dmitry Bivol — once each — and Terence Crawford jumped two full divisions from 154 to face Canelo at 168. WBC complicity documented.

Lightweight · Current
Gervonta Davis vs. Shakur Stevenson
Duck Call: Tank

Two of the best lightweights of their generation — one from Baltimore, one from Newark — and the fight never got made. Overlapping weights. Years of public demand. Tank’s record of avoidance is frequently cited alongside Shakur, Devin Haney, and Vasyl Lomachenko, and his career has been defined as much by inactivity as by performance — his last three fights came in March 2025, June 2024, and April 2023.

The legal situation remains unresolved. Davis was arrested in Miami in late January 2026 on charges of attempted kidnapping, false imprisonment, and battery stemming from an October 2025 incident involving his ex-girlfriend at a Miami area club. He posted bond and has been out since. Separately, a Baltimore City Circuit Judge denied a motion to recall an active arrest warrant in May 2026 for violating probation from his 2020 Baltimore hit-and-run case. That warrant remains live. The WBA has designated him champion in recess.

Meanwhile Shakur, in January 2026, publicly stated “I’m a big superstar… I don’t need him” — which his critics have used to argue the avoidance runs both directions. The mechanism: a PBC promotional wall vs. Matchroom, compounded by Davis’s legal limbo.

Junior Welterweight / Welterweight · Current
Shakur Stevenson vs. Devin Haney
No Duck Call — Bilateral Standoff
Devin Haney · Shakur Stevenson · June 10, 2026 — agreed, then didn’t

Two unbeaten American technicians with no clean avoidance story — just a fight that keeps not getting made. Stevenson beat Teofimo Lopez by unanimous decision on January 31, 2026, at Madison Square Garden, capturing the WBO and Ring magazine junior welterweight titles and becoming a four-division world champion. Haney holds the WBO welterweight title, won over Brian Norman Jr. in November 2025.

On June 10, 2026, the two appeared to negotiate and agree to a fight live on social media, only to pull back within minutes. The proposed meeting point was 144 pounds — Stevenson cited the Mayweather-Canelo catchweight as precedent. It collapsed immediately: Haney accused Stevenson of “fake public negotiations,” and Stevenson fired back that real negotiations happen offline. Now a compounding structural block: the WBO has ordered Haney to defend against mandatory challenger Keyshawn Davis by August 2026, which pushes any Stevenson fight further back regardless of what the two fighters want.

Status: Negotiation Standoff · Not Dead
Super Welterweight · Current
Jaron “Boots” Ennis vs. Vergil Ortiz Jr.
Duck Call: Promotional Structure

Ennis moved to 154 pounds in October 2025, stopping Uisma Lima in one round for the WBA interim super welterweight title. After Ortiz stopped Erickson Lubin in two rounds in Fort Worth in November 2025, Ortiz called Ennis into the ring for a public face-off, declaring him next. Terms were agreed between both camps, with Eddie Hearn confirming it — but stopping short of guaranteeing it would happen.

The mechanism that killed it: Ortiz filed a federal lawsuit against Golden Boy Promotions in January 2026, arguing that when Golden Boy’s broadcast deal with DAZN expired on December 31, 2025, he became a free agent and was entitled to sign with Matchroom to make the Ennis fight. Golden Boy fought back, maintaining their promotional contract remained valid independent of the broadcast deal. A Nevada judge sided with Golden Boy in March 2026, compelling arbitration and blocking Ortiz from negotiating with outside parties until the dispute resolves — with the arbitrator asked to settle by September.

“I did everything in my power to make this fight happen for the fans. I waited long enough and I stayed quiet through it all. It looks like Vergil or his team really didn’t want to fight.” — Boots Ennis, March 12, 2026

Both fighters wanted this fight. The lawsuit is the mechanism.

Heavyweight · Current
Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua
Duck Call: Joshua Signed on Paper · Unfought in the Ring
Tottenham Hotspur Stadium · April 11, 2026 · Fury in the ring, Joshua ringside · The moment in one frame

The fight is signed. Following Fury’s win over Arslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on April 11, 2026, Saudi boxing power broker Turki Alalshikh confirmed: “It’s happening. It’s signed.” Eddie Hearn added: “Signed, sealed, delivered. AJ v Fury is on.” Wembley Stadium, Q4 2026, November the target date. Joshua fights Kristian Prenga in Riyadh on July 25 as a tune-up.

It is still on this page.

This fight has been “happening” before. Contracts have been signed before. Dates have been targeted before. The entire history of Fury-Joshua is a masterclass in how a fight can be real on paper and never happen in a ring. The April 2026 Tottenham moment — Fury calling Joshua out in the ring, Joshua sitting ringside filming on his phone and staying seated — is the most recent entry in a long pattern. The signing is noted. The fight is not yet fought.

Status: Signed on Paper · Unfought in the Ring
Minimumweight · Current
Oscar Collazo vs. Pedro Taduran
Duck Call: Collazo

Oscar Collazo holds the WBO, WBA, and Ring magazine minimumweight titles. Pedro Taduran holds the IBF belt. Collazo has repeatedly chosen lower-ranked opponents for his title defenses rather than pursue Taduran — his June 20, 2026 defense at the Frontwave Arena in Oceanside, California is against Joey Canoy, ranked No. 9 by the WBA.

Taduran, as of late May 2026, stated he is waiting to see what happens after Collazo’s Canoy fight before making his next move, still holding out hope for a unification. Taduran’s promoter Sean Gibbons has been actively seeking a unification fight with Collazo’s team at Golden Boy. The mechanism is a champion consistently selecting easier defenses over the available unification fight.
